subject: Re: Eval plan & dataset format for FinServe POC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finserve.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 14:02:00 -0000
Subject: Follow-up: Eval plan & dataset format for FinServe POC

Hi Laura — great to meet earlier. Thanks again to you and James for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the eval environment.

Recap from discovery:
- Primary goal: assess model fit for transaction categorization + explanation generation on FinServe customer support transcripts (low-latency inference requirement, strong correctness bar on categories).
- Data constraints: sample records contain PII; FinServe needs KMS + encryption at rest/in transit for POC.
- Success criteria: >= 92% category accuracy (automated metric) and average human rating >= 4/5 on explanation quality.

Recommended eval plan (initial):
1) Models to include:
   - llama-3-13b (quantized q4f16) — baseline for instruction quality
   - mistral-7b-instruct (int8) — strong price/latency tradeoff
   - redwood-1.3b-instruct (fp16) — low-cost control run
2) Dataset: 500 labeled examples (we can start with 200 if needed) in JSONL format (see attached redwood-eval-template.jsonl). Each record: id, input, expected_output, metadata.
3) Scoring: automated category accuracy + token-level and string-similarity metrics for explanations (exact match when applicable, ROUGE-L for free-text), plus a small blind human eval (n=50) for quality/regression checks.
4) Timeline: once dataset & SOW are signed, we can kick off infra + evals in ~3 business days and have first results in ~5 business days.

Attachments: finserve-prompt-set.csv (initial prompts / edge cases), redwood-eval-template.jsonl (dataset schema), SOW-draft.pdf (initial SOW).

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm an initial dataset of ~200-500 examples and share a Drive link?
- Can you confirm procurement/legal contact so we can send the SOW?
- Any must-have tests (e.g., fairness slices, latency SLOs) beyond the criteria above?

I copied Neha and Dev to help with technical setup and infra/PII notes. Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if that helps.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0178

---
Attachment stubs:
- finserve-prompt-set.csv (CSV, 28 rows)
- redwood-eval-template.jsonl (JSONL, template)
- SOW-draft.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finserve.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 15:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Eval plan & dataset format for FinServe POC

Hi Laura — great, I can confirm we have view access to the Drive link. Answers below inline.

PII/BYOK: Neha — can you confirm BYOK + log-disable options for POC?

Human scoring rubric (summary):
- 1-5 quality rating (1 = incorrect/misleading, 5 = correct & helpful) for explanation quality.
- Pass/fail flag for regulatory risk (binary).
- Automated metrics: category accuracy (primary), exact match (%) for canonical outputs, ROUGE-L for free-text explanations.
- Aggregation: we report per-slice metrics (by product, transaction size, and channel) and overall metrics.

Dataset format (attached template highlights):
- JSONL lines with fields: "id" (string), "input" (string), "expected_output" (string), "metadata" (JSON string with keys: product, channel, contains_pii:true/false). Example record (single-line JSONL):
  {"id":"fin-0001","input":"Customer: I was charged twice for invoice 12345, please explain." ,"expected_output":"Category: Billing Error; Explanation: Customer was charged twice due to duplicate invoice run on 2027-05-02. Refund issued.","metadata":"{\"product\":\"Payments\",\"channel\":\"email\",\"contains_pii\":true}"}

We recommend masking direct identifiers in the POC dataset (replace account numbers with token placeholders) if possible. If you need us to run an internal redaction step we can do that as part of the ingest.

Timeline: If you send final dataset + procurement sign-off within 48 hours, we can meet the July 10 result target (we'll prioritize the POC run).

I'll also attach the redwood-eval-template.jsonl — the team will use that to run the automated and human evals.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment stub: redwood-eval-template.jsonl (shows schema + scoring defaults)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Eval plan & dataset format for FinServe POC

Hi all — quick tech notes from infra/secure-setup perspective: 

- BYOK: confirmed. We can provision a customer-managed key via AWS KMS or a provided encryption key; logs can be disabled for the POC environment and access scoped to a small set of service accounts.
- Data handling: recommend masking direct identifiers before upload. If FinServe prefers, we can run a short redaction pipeline on our side (requires an additional signed data transfer addendum).
- Model sizing: for the 300-example run we recommend starting with the three models Marissa listed. Expected run duration (wall time): ~3-5 hours total for automated metrics on dedicated infra (GPU pool), plus 1-2 business days for the blind human eval (we use a small QA panel).
- Cost note: rough POC compute estimate = $1.2k-–$2.5k depending on model mix and whether you want priority capacity. We can provide a more detailed breakdown in the SOW.
- Attached eval-config.yaml includes: eval slices, metric thresholds, and the instruction prompts used for each model run.

If procurement confirms SOW send to procurement@finserve.com we'll attach the infra addendum and kick provisioning.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Attachment stub: eval-config.yaml (YAML, 1 file)
